content:
maria: Heads-up — CoreTech is hitting hard rate limits during an SSO integration POC. They asked for temporary relief because their test harness spikes when replaying sessions.
maria: Request came in from partner-eng at 09:12 PT: "Can you give us a short window of elevated throughput for integration testing?"
josh: When's the window and typical shape of the traffic?
maria: They want a 2h window starting ~3pm PT today. Pattern is bursty: many small requests for embeddings + occasional chat completions. We're seeing 429s and queueing.
kevin: Which API key/org? Any red flags on past abuse?
maria: Org: coretech-inc, key: rk_live_[redacted]. No prior abuse, but they have a heavy embedding workload.
ellie: Proposal: short-lived allowlist entry for the key with explicit token quota and burst cap. Also attach a billing tag and an auto-expire.
josh: Agree. Minimum controls: (1) fixed token quota for the window, (2) burst cap to avoid starving other tenants, (3) telemetry hooks to watch p95 latency and 429 rate.
kevin: I can add an allowlist record in permit-service. Suggest config below — TTL 24h to be safe: 
```json
{
  "scope": "api_key",
  "subject": "rk_live_[redacted]",
  "limits": {
    "rate_per_min": 7200,
    "burst": 1500,
    "token_quota": 900000
  },
  "expires_at": "2026-03-30T20:00:00Z",
  "note": "expedited partner POC - CoreTech; support ticket S-8923"
}
```
maria: That looks good. Can we also make the allowlist scoped so it only applies to embedding endpoints? We don't want to open completions as well.
kevin: Yep — permit-service supports endpoint scoping. I'll include `endpoints: ["/v1/embeddings"]`.
ellie: Add an automated post-expiry job that flips the org into a denylist if usage exceeded expected thresholds. We need to avoid silent overrun.
josh: I'll own the billing side: tag usages with `poc-partner:coretech` and set an alert at 80% of the token_quota. If breached, notify billing + eng-platform.
maria: Oncall: any objections to a manual allowlist for this key? @kevin to PR and @deploy-bot to roll.
kevin: I'll PR the migration to add the entry and the UI support for TTL. PR: https://github.com/redwood/permit/pull/412 — includes audit logging and endpoint scoping.
deploy-bot: deploy started for permit-service (allowlist/ttl) — canary -> rolling
kevin: Applied config to staging. Will apply to prod after canary passes.
maria: Observability: please add a temporary dashboard (or a grafana panel) with per-key p50/p95 latency, 429 rate, queue_length, and token consumption. Link it here when ready.
ellie: I'll add a panel and a quick alert rule. Will create: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/partner-poc/coretech (placeholder)
josh: Support runbook to send partner: expected TTL, billing note, contact point, and fallback behavior (if we start throttling we'll route to smaller model variant or return 429).
maria: Also require an audit ticket with the business justification (partner POC) + signoff. support-bot, please create.
support-bot: Created ticket S-8923 (priority: high) — assigned to josh. Reminder scheduled for 24h to review and remove allowlist if present.
josh: I'll monitor usage and billing. If they go beyond agreed quota we bill and discuss with Sales.
kevin: Canary looks healthy. I'll promote to prod now. Prod apply time: 1862345800.
maria: Great. Once live, send a note to partner-eng and product ops. Also, add a post-mortem step to evaluate whether we should offer a lightweight Partner POC tier in the console.
ellie: Side note: we should standardize the temporary allowlist flow in the console (templated TTL, quota presets) — prevents ad-hoc PRs. Filing a tiny RFC.
maria: Thanks, team. Closing loop: partner notified, runbook sent, allowlist applied, monitoring in place. Will reconvene after the window for a short review. :thumbsup:
